newsitem.title: FRANCE: France tries to ease tension with U.S. over snub.
newsitem.headline: France tries to ease tension with U.S. over snub.

text.p: France tried on Friday to ease tension with the United States over a reported snub by Foreign Minister Herve de Charette of his outgoing U.S. counterpart Warren Christopher.

"We don't wish a controversy and all we have to say is we want to develop our relations with the United States, which have always been based on friendship and the defence of common values," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
The row broke out on Thursday when the Washington Post newspaper said De Charette had walked out during a toast in honour of Christopher at a NATO function in Brussels earlier in the week.
Paris, backed by NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, initially denied outright there was any substance to the story.
But the U.S. State Department later confirmed the American press account and a U.S. official said de Charette had been "extremely discourteous".
De Charette's office then took a new tack and said he had not deliberately snubbed Christopher. A senior French official told Reuters that Solana's tribute had not been on the agenda.

The controversy reflected the raw state of Franco-U.S. relations, with disputes accumulating over the reform of NATO's military structure, the succession to U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, France's drive for a bigger say in the Middle East and sharp differences over Western policy on Zaire.

"The whole thing (about the Brussels incident) is derisory," Rummelhardt said during Friday's daily press brefing. "The relations between Warren Christopher and Herve de Charette have always been warm and courteous."

Christopher and De Charette are likely to meet again in Washington on Monday at a meeting of the Friends of Lebanon, a group of 30 countries including the United States and France devoted to giving Lebanon financial aid for reconstruction.
"Herve de Charette will be there and Warren Christopher should be there too," Rummelhardt said.
